implementation_notes: The Python default keeps the domain as plain classes or dataclasses and lets SQLAlchemy map them from outside: Table objects are declared with the schema, and registry.map_imperatively(Order, order_table, properties={...}) attaches the mapping afterwards, so the model classes carry no declarative base, no Column and no relationship descriptors. SQLAlchemy's own documentation calls this the imperative (formerly 'classical') mapping and stresses that the mapped class includes no declarative attributes - the ORM depends on the model instead of the model on the ORM. The Mapper is provided by the library; you only write the explicit configuration and a start_mappers() entry point, and the classic hand-written mapper is reserved for models SQLAlchemy cannot map automatically (multi-attribute value objects spread over columns).
code_sketch:
# domain/model.py
@dataclass
class Order:
    id: OrderId
    lines: list[OrderLine]
    def confirm(self) -> None: ...

# infrastructure/orm.py - the only module importing sqlalchemy
order_table = Table("orders", metadata,
                    Column("id", String, primary_key=True))
mapper_registry.map_imperatively(
    Order, order_table, properties={"lines": relationship(OrderLine)})
pitfalls: Implicit imports: if any domain module imports the orm module (even indirectly for type hints), the dependency inversion is gone - keep start_mappers() called from the composition root only.

Dataclass identity vs the identity map: generated __eq__ compares by value while the ORM tracks by identity, so equality, sets and caching behave differently for loaded objects (frozen dataclasses and explicit id-based equals avoid surprises).
Lazy loading after the session closed raises DetachedInstanceError, and loading relations implicitly during mapping produces N+1 queries.
Validating in __post_init__ or factories is required: the dataclass constructor the ORM calls is generated and will happily build invalid objects from bad rows.

variants.name: Dataclasses with a hand-written mapper inside the repository
variants.implementation_notes: For models that SQLAlchemy's imperative mapping cannot express automatically - multi-attribute value objects, aggregates spread over several tables, Django or raw-SQL stores - the mapper is written by hand: a pair of functions (order_model_to_entity, order_entity_to_model) next to the repository, or a Pydantic entity built with model_validate(row, from_attributes=True) when the boundary schema matters. The repository then returns domain objects only; this costs explicit code per field but keeps the entity constructor in charge of validation and works with any storage library.
pitfalls: Pydantic and dataclass constructors are bypassed by ORM/validation shortcuts (model_validate with from_attributes copies attributes; JSON round-trips too) - validate in __post_init__ or the model factory.
Mapping functions drift: without round-trip tests a renamed column silently becomes a missing value or a defaults-filled domain object.
